refuted_claims:
Each item below gives the claim, what I checked (training cells only, no model calls), and what I found. My scripts are in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-dulin-Documents-Paper-SkillOpt/e7258b97-b430-4dd5-959d-eb871e7c777f/scratchpad/feas/D11-critic/scripts/.

1. Claim: "So the task card halves the run noise" (evidence A).
- Checked: run-to-run disagreement within one arm (K=2) for byte-identical requests in the v3 rounds.
- Found: it holds only in the cal-1 window (seed 0.049 vs scaffold 0.104-0.119).
- In v3 the SearchQA seed scored 0.090 (I-ds s1 train) and the scaffold 0.035 (E-ds s1 train). In the same terse window the seed was 0.035 (I-ds s1 screen), equal to the scaffold.
- The OfficeQA seed ranged 0.067-0.183 across five rounds with identical requests. LiveMath: seed 0.160 vs scaffold 0.130. ALFWorld: 0.140 vs 0.140.
- So π_rep depends on the window by a factor of 2-3. Borrowed π (the R5 fallback) and every projected floor and MDE carry that uncertainty, and none is shown.

2. Claim: "SearchQA n=400 MDE80 3.5-4.4; per bench 3.5-10; macro 3.5-3.8" (F and verdict_cn).
- Checked: projections.py and my own K-subset SEs.
- The upper end, 4.4, comes from the v3 seed-vs-scaffold contrast, which was 0% co-scheduled; the explorer's own R8 would refuse it a CI.
- The co-scheduled cal-1 contrast gives 5.6 at K=1. That is the explorer's own section-A number; I recomputed K=1 SE 2.84 at n=200, which gives 5.6 at n=400.
- Every MDE uses unadjusted α=0.05, yet R4 makes Holm over 10 cells the test. The first rejection then needs p<0.005, a multiplier of 3.65 instead of 2.80 (×1.30).
- Corrected: SearchQA about 4.6-7.3, OfficeQA about 8.2-9.6, LiveMath, SpreadsheetBench and ALFWorld about 11.6-12.9 points.

3. Claim: "frequentist paired intervals are fine at stage-table sizes" (Wald-t 94.6-95.7% at n≥125).
- Their grid leaves out discordance below 8% and Δ ≥ discordance; the code has `if delta >= disc: skip`.
- I enumerated the multinomial exactly at those points:

| n | Discordance | Δ (points) | Wald-t coverage |
|---|---|---|---|
| 125 | 2% | 1 | 84.2% |
| 172 | 2% | 2 | 85.8% |
| 400 | 2% | 2 | 89.5% |
| 125 | 4% | 3 | 92.5% |
| 125 | 8% | 8 | 93.0% |
| 172 | 8% | 8 | 92.7% |

- Tango covered 93.4-98.9% at the same points.
- This is exactly the headline Δ-vs-Seed situation: same-text disagreement for the seed is 0.03-0.09. R3's switch to Tango is needed, and it is not in the code.

4. Claim: "implemented and verified" template.
- Checked: stage_table.py and d11stats.py.
- (a) R8 is not implemented: there is no "not co-scheduled, no CI" and no "reused, Δ≡0". Demo B prints CIs beside "NoSkill NO (overlap 0%)", and evidence D quotes them.
- (b) The R3 Tango switch, the R6/R7 sensitivity flags, the R10 transfer and non-inferiority verdicts, and the R11 placebo column are all missing.
- (c) The R4 p-value, `signflip_test(d)`, flips single items rather than OfficeQA clusters, while the CI is CR1. This contradicts R1 and is anti-conservative when items from the same file are correlated.
- (d) The overlap rule (shared span ÷ shorter window ≥ 0.8) accepts a short arm nested inside a long arm, even when most of the long arm's cells ran in another regime.

5. The decision rules conflict.
- R10 uses the unadjusted t-CI bound; R4 uses a Holm-adjusted sign-flip p, which is a different test.
- Demo B ALFWorld: CI [+2.3, +18.7] excludes 0, but p_Holm = 0.103.
- Registered cal-1 control:1: CI [−6.34, −0.66] excludes 0, but sign-test p = 0.098.
- The Δ-vs-NoSkill cells, declared "context only", still sit in the Holm family and dilute the headline column.

6. Claim: "Re-running a non-co-scheduled contrast costs one arm per bench (~1.4M)".
- Co-scheduling needs both arms in the new window.
- Measured cost per cell for the seed (v3 training): SearchQA 3.9k, OfficeQA 8.4k, LiveMath 4.4k, SpreadsheetBench 4.3k, ALFWorld 116k (scaffold 29k).
- Re-measuring the v3 table (NoSkill, I-ds, E-ds) costs about 32M tokens.
- Each changed stage of a future run needs NoSkill, Seed and Final, plus the previous Final for the registered step-change readout. That is about 46-66M per stage vs about 20M today, i.e. 2.3-3.3× the test cost. cost_estimate does not include this.

7. R11 uses ONE placebo arm.
- cal-1's four placebos ranged from −9.75 to +3.62 (SD 5.7 points), wider than any per-bench MDE. A single placebo is one draw from that spread.
- Those placebos were scaffold + placebo text; the effect on top of the Seed was never measured. At least 3-4 texts are needed, at about 4.5M each (about 20M with ALFWorld).

8. Claim: "naive SE wrong in either direction".
- In all 10 cal-1 contrasts the naive-to-paired ratio is 1.01-2.29. Only conservatism is shown.

9. Claim: "regime × text interaction −6.00 [−10.45, −1.55]".
- That figure compares a non-co-scheduled estimate with an interleaved one, so it measures the scaffold's regime shift.
- It reads as an interaction on SearchQA only because the seed happens to be regime-robust there:
  - Seed, terse vs verbose window: +0.25 [−2.91, +3.41].
  - Seed − scaffold, both terse: +3.50 [+0.33, +6.67], against +9.38 interleaved.
- On OfficeQA the sensitive arm is the seed (−24), and the scaffold was never measured in a verbose window.
- On LiveMath, SpreadsheetBench and ALFWorld, same-item seed contrasts across windows were −1.8 to +3.4, so no regime effect was detected. The sentinel's terse signature tells nothing about those three benches.

10. Literature.
- The "correction" of the clustered SE from Eq. 8 to Eq. 4 is backwards. Miller Eq. 8 is the paired, cluster-adjusted SE computed from differences, which is exactly the template's sum; Eq. 4 is for a single mean.
- He 2025 explains token-level flips, not a two-mode switch of about 70 points in terse share. The closer precedents are Chen 2023 and Yuan et al. 2025 (arXiv:2506.09501).
- Bowyer Sec. 3.4 says all non-Bayesian methods undercover for small N in paired comparisons; "agrees with Bowyer" is true only for n ≤ 20.

11. Recommendation 4 does not fit the owner's yardstick.
- "Claim +4 on the macro row": the macro averages the trained bench with similar and dissimilar benches. A +4 effect on two similar targets shows as +1.6 on the macro.
- "More items are the fix": the test pools are fixed (OfficeQA 172, LiveMath 125), and K is the only lever there.
confirmed_claims:
These I recomputed independently or checked at the source.

cal-1 (cell extract identical to the old-machine copy; registered analysis.json present):
- 8,800/8,800 cells have verdicts; 15 unknown; 8 truncated.
- π_rep:

| Arm | π_rep (items) | ICC |
|---|---|---|
| parent:A | 0.1187 (198) | 0.73 |
| parent:B | 0.1035 (198) | 0.76 |
| parent:A+B pooled | 0.1075 (196) | |
| ids-full | 0.0494 (199) | 0.86 |
| seed-only | 0.0516 | |
| cand | 0.157 | |
| placebos | 0.074-0.161 | |

- Design effects 2.29 / 1.23 / 1.01.
- K-subset SE for ids-full − parent:A: 2.84 / 2.43 / 2.20 (explorer 2.82 / 2.44 / 2.22); ω² = 0.077; MDE80 at n=400 5.6 / 4.8 / 4.4.

Verification and tests:
- I re-ran verify_vs_registered: ALL MATCH, 10/10.
- Unit tests: 42/42 with the repo root as argument (39 without it). The repo's git status is unchanged.

Request identity:
- 1,213 recurring (text, item) pairs, 9,707 first sends, 0 with more than one hash.
- max_tokens is always 32768; cal-1 and v3 requests are byte-identical.
- reasoning_chars is always 0; returned_model never changes; n_sends is about 1, so retries are not the cause.

Occasion effects (same text, same items):
- OfficeQA seed on 60 items: s3 screen − s2 train +22.50 [+11.49, +33.51] (17 up / 2 down); s3 − s4 screen +24.17 [+12.64, +35.69]; s4 screen vs s4 confirm 0.0 [−6.73, +6.73].
- SearchQA scaffold: v3 − cal-1 +6.4 [+2.3, +10.4]; s1 screen − s1 train −5.5 [−9.6, −1.4]. Seed v3 vs cal-1: +0.25.
- The 15-minute terse-share timeline reproduces.

Other checks:
- Demo B SearchQA +3.25 [−0.39, +6.89] (20 up / 11 down) reproduces.
- Small-n coverage, my simulation: n=6 t 80-94%, bootstrap 54-78%; n=11 89-96% / 74-86%; n=20 94-97% / 87-90%. Banning the bootstrap on trigger panels is justified.
- A grid spot check matches theirs (n=125, 8% discordance, Δ=3 points: 0.946).
- Literature verified: Miller Eq. 1, 4, 7, 9, 10 and the (1+2/K)/3 factor in Sec. 3.1; Bowyer's title, ICML 2025 spotlight and Sec. 3.1, 3.2, 3.4; Madaan's claims; the Newcombe Table III values; Tango and Holm.
- Rule compliance: the path guard holds, no test path was touched, and there were 0 model calls.
- Owner constraints: a headline Δ vs the task-card Seed and a sentinel made only of training items do not breach the no-validation-set or good-instruction rules.
missing:
- An OfficeQA sign-flip test at cluster (source-file) level.
- The McNemar mid-p test (Fagerland et al. 2013/2014) for single-run tables with few discordant items.
- Intervals consistent with Holm, or one small pre-named primary family, for example Δ vs Seed on the registered similar targets.
- A macro that leaves out the trained bench, plus self / similar / rest class rows using the registered readout (skillopt/coevo5/readout.py transfer_cells, Q1-Q3 one-sided bounds). Co-scheduled step changes ΔA[s][b].
- Uncertainty bands on the projected noise floors and MDEs (π_rep varies 2-3× across windows).
- Serving identity per send: receipts store only status, finish_reason, returned_model, reasoning_chars, seconds and usage. Add system_fingerprint, response id and headers. The latency field ('seconds') is already recorded and was never tested as a free regime marker.
- A check of the OfficeQA scaffold in a verbose window before the sentinel relies on it.
- An owner view: a simple stage-by-stage five-bench table, with the 13-column block moved to an appendix.
- References: Card 2020 (power), Dror 2018 (significance testing in NLP), Sclar 2024 and Mizrahi 2024 (prompt-format sensitivity, prior evidence for placebo effects), Yuan 2025.
notes_cn: 复核结论：方向成立，主要数字能复现，但有几处说过头。我独立重算了校准实验的数字，也重算了“同样的请求在不同时间段会得到简短或啰嗦两种回答”和“OfficeQA（文档问答）同题同文字分数差22到24分”，都属实。问题有四个。一，“任务说明让重跑波动减半”只在校准那个时间段成立，换个时间段不成立。二，“单个评测集能检出3.5到10分”偏乐观，按同时段数据并做多项检验的校正，约为5到13分。三，程序有几条规则没真正做到，例如不同时段跑的对比照样给出区间。四，每张表要三个版本同时段重跑，测试花费约为现在的2到3倍，原估算漏了；只放一份无关文字作对照也不够。
